message.content:
Let \(n=|a|\). Every positive divisor \(d\) of \(n\) gives two integer divisors of \(a\): \(d\) and \(-d\).

If the positive divisors of \(n\) are \(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_k\), then the product of all divisors of \(a\) is

\[
(d_1d_2\cdots d_k)\cdot(-d_1)(-d_2)\cdots(-d_k)
=(-1)^k (d_1d_2\cdots d_k)^2.
\]

The square factor is positive, so the product is negative exactly when \(k\), the number of positive divisors of \(n\), is odd.

A positive integer has an odd number of divisors exactly when it is a perfect square. Thus we need \(|a|\) to be a perfect square between \(1\) and \(200\).

The perfect squares in this range are

\[
1^2,2^2,\dots,14^2
\]

since \(14^2=196\le 200\) and \(15^2=225>200\).

So there are \(14\) such integers \(a\).

The answer is 14.
